items.name: Squat
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Sit back and down, chest up
Knees track over your toes
items.why: Strong quads and glutes absorb each landing, so your knees don't have to.

items.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold the weight at your chest
Elbows inside the knees at the bottom
Drive up through the whole foot
items.why: Loaded squats build the strength that holds your form late in a race.

items.name: Reverse lunge
cues: Step back, both knees to 90°
Front shin stays upright
Push through the front heel to stand
items.why: Running is one leg at a time: this trains each side on its own.

items.name: Bulgarian split squat
cues: Back foot on the bench, laces down
Lower straight down, torso tall
Front knee over the middle of the foot
items.why: The best single-leg strength builder for hills and the final kilometres.

items.name: Single-leg deadlift
cues: Hinge at the hip, back flat
Free leg reaches back in line with your body
Hips stay square to the floor
items.why: Hamstring strength and balance on one leg: fewer pulls, steadier stride.

items.name: Romanian deadlift
cues: Soft knees, push the hips back
Weights slide down close to the legs
Stand tall by squeezing the glutes
items.why: Strong posterior chain: more push-off, less load on the lower back.

items.name: Glute bridge
cues: Feet flat, knees bent
Lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up
Squeeze the glutes at the top for a second
items.why: Wakes up the glutes so they, not your lower back, drive your stride.

items.name: Single-leg bridge
cues: One foot down, the other leg straight
Hips stay level as you lift
Pause at the top
items.why: Each glute on its own, as in running: evens out a weaker side.

items.name: Calf raise
cues: Rise onto the balls of your feet
Pause at the top
Lower slowly, three seconds
items.why: Your calves take several times your body weight with every step.

items.name: Single-leg calf raise
cues: Stand on one foot, a hand on the wall
Straight knee, all the way up
Three seconds down
items.why: Protects the Achilles and calves, the most common runner niggles.

items.name: Plank
cues: Elbows under the shoulders
One straight line from head to heels
Breathe, don't hold your breath
items.why: A stiff trunk passes force from your legs instead of leaking it.

items.name: Push-up
cues: Hands just wider than the shoulders
Body in one line, core tight
Chest close to the floor, then press
items.why: Upper-body strength keeps your arm drive and posture late in long runs.

items.name: Dead bug
cues: Lower back pressed into the floor
Reach the opposite arm and leg away
Move slowly, breathe out as you reach
items.why: Teaches your core to stay still while arms and legs move: running.

items.name: Bird dog
cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Reach the opposite arm and leg long
Keep the hips level, no twisting
items.why: Back and glute control for a steady pelvis on every stride.

items.name: Jump squat
cues: Quarter squat, then jump tall
Land softly through the balls of the feet
Reset before the next one
items.why: Springiness: more speed for the same effort.

items.name: Pogo hops
cues: Small, quick hops on the balls of the feet
Knees almost straight, stiff ankles
Quiet landings
items.why: Trains the ankle spring that makes running economical.

items.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
cues: Kneel in a lunge, back knee down
Tuck the pelvis, squeeze the back glute
Shift forward until the front of the hip stretches
items.why: Opens hips that sitting tightens, for a longer, easier stride.

items.name: Back squat
cues: Bar on your upper back, hands just outside the shoulders
Brace, then sit down between your hips
Drive up, chest and hips rising together
items.why: The heaviest leg strength you can build: more push in every stride and sturdier knees.

items.name: Deadlift
cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins close to it
Flat back, push the floor away
Hips and shoulders rise together; stand tall
items.why: Strengthens the whole back of the body that holds your posture late in a run.

items.name: Bench press
cues: Eyes under the bar, feet planted
Lower to mid-chest, elbows at about 45°
Press up and slightly back
items.why: Upper-body strength for a strong arm drive and a balanced body.

items.name: Overhead press
cues: Bar on your collarbones, grip just outside the shoulders
Squeeze your glutes, press straight up
Head through at the top
items.why: Strong shoulders on a stable trunk: good posture when you tire.

items.name: Bent-over row
cues: Hinge to about 45°, back flat
Pull the bar to your lower ribs
Lower it under control
items.why: Pulling strength that keeps your upper back from rounding late in a race.

items.name: Pull-up
cues: Hang on straight arms, hands a little wider than the shoulders
Pull your chest to the bar
Lower all the way, slowly
items.why: The best upper-body pull there is: a strong back and arms that hold your form.

items.name: Biceps curl
cues: Elbows by your sides
Curl up, palms to your shoulders
Lower slowly
items.why: Arm strength for a strong swing on hills and sprints.

items.name: Lateral raise
cues: A little bend in the elbows
Raise out to shoulder height
Lead with the elbows; lower slowly
items.why: Healthy, strong shoulders that carry your arm swing.

items.name: Hip thrust
cues: Upper back on the bench, bar over your hips
Drive through your heels to a straight line
Ribs down; squeeze at the top
items.why: Glute power for hills and the last kilometres.

items.name: Kettlebell swing
cues: Hike the bell back between your legs
Snap your hips through
Let it float to chest height
items.why: Explosive hips: a faster, springier stride.

items.name: Step-up
cues: Whole foot on the box
Drive up through the top leg, not the back one
Step down slowly
items.why: Single-leg strength the way running uses it: one leg lifting you up.

items.name: Side plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder
Hips up, a straight line head to feet
Breathe; don't let the hips sag
items.why: Stops the hip dropping on every stride.

items.name: Bench dip
cues: Hands on the edge behind you, fingers forward
Lower until your elbows reach 90°
Press back up, shoulders down
items.why: Arm and shoulder strength with nothing but a bench.

items.name: Mountain climbers
cues: Hands under the shoulders, body long
Drive the knees to your chest in turn
Keep the hips level
items.why: Core and quick knee drive, with your heart rate up.

items.name: Crunch
cues: Knees bent, feet flat
Curl your shoulders off the floor
Lower slowly; don't pull on your neck
items.why: A strong front of the trunk to hold your posture.
